In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immunological characteristics of cells which enter the liver via the portal blood.
the immunology of the liver, and in particular the immunological characteristics of the cells entering the liver from the blood.
the immunological and physiological aspects of the liver as an organ and with the mechanisms by which the liver influences the host immune response.

the liver is not a passive organ, but an organ with an active immune surveillance system.
the liver is an important immunological organ, which is not only involved in the immune response to foreign antigens but also has an important role in the immune response against self-antigens.
the spleen is the major site for the production of mononuclear phagocytes and lymphocytes that enter the liver via the portal blood and that the liver is the site of their maturation and activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spleen is the major source of cells entering the sinusoids of the liver.
the liver is a major organ of immunological activity and that the spleen is a source of immunological cells entering the liver.
the spleen, the mesentery, and the liver are the major sites where lymphocytes are activated, expanded, and differentiated, and that the liver is a major site of lymphocyte recirculation.

the spleen is the main source of the cells entering the liver.
